title: Granular tenant fencing and soft-quota rebalance proposal
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Summary: After the capacity incident on 2026-02-14 we observed repeated eviction cascades tied to a small subset of tenants that intermittently consumed large token bursts and exhausted shared burst budgets. Prior tickets focused on reservation sizing and coarse throttles; this proposal describes a granular tenant fencing strategy plus a soft-quota rebalance mechanism to reduce eviction frequency while preserving burstability for healthy tenants.

Goals: (1) Prevent tenant-driven eviction cascades that impact other tenants in dedicated clusters. (2) Reduce surface area for operator interventions by enabling automatic soft rebalances instead of hard evictions. (3) Keep application-visible latency and throughput SLOs within target during normal and bursty patterns.

Scope: Implementation spans runtime admission controller, reservation allocator, and autoscaling policy hooks. No user-facing API changes. This is platform-internal and will be feature-flagged per-cluster.

Proposed controls and rationale: 
- Capacity fencing (soft fences): allocate a per-tenant dynamic headroom percentage that grows/shrinks based on recent burst volatility rather than fixed hard quotas. Rationale: hard fences caused abrupt evictions during transient spikes. Soft fences reserve less capacity for stable tenants while protecting neighbors from recurring heavy hitters.
- Token shedding window: introduce a short, probabilistic token-shedding mechanism when a tenant exceeds a moving-window burst score to avoid single-request blow-ups from abusing burst tokens. Rationale: token shedding smooths burst arrival rates and buys time for autoscaler to react.
- Soft-quota rebalance: when cluster-level reservation utilization exceeds a high-water mark, trigger an automated rebalance that reduces soft-headroom for low-risk tenants and temporarily tightens soft fences for high-risk tenants rather than evicting.
- Burst smoothing policy: rate-limit large multi-token requests at the serving runtime with a prioritized backoff that degrades throughput gradually rather than dropping connections.
- Telemetry and scoring: compute a "burst volatility" score per tenant using recent 1m/5m/1h token-rate variances, eviction_count, and KV cache miss ratio. Use score to drive fence aggressiveness.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Canary: deploy to one dedicated cluster with 30 representative tenants for 7 days. No cluster-level eviction spike > 10x baseline; P95 latency for number-gen endpoints remains within +15% of baseline; customers in canary show no customer-facing errors attributable to quota enforcement.
- Production: after canary validation, roll to 25% of clusters with auto rollback on metric regressions.

Rollback plan: Feature-flagged. If evictions increase or latency regressions exceed thresholds during rollout, immediately revert the feature flag and scale up reservations temporarily while investigating.

Telemetry & dashboards required: new cluster-level and tenant-level dashboards for reservation_utilization, eviction_count, burst_volatility_score, shed_events, and token_shed_rate. Alerts on reservation_utilization > 92% sustained for 5m, eviction_count spike > 3x baseline in 10m, or shed_events impacting > 5 tenants in 1m.

Operational runbook snippets: 
- When shed_events alert fires: identify top 5 tenants by shed_events, increase their fence aggressiveness to prevent further shedding, and open a support ticket with tenant owners.
- If eviction_count alert fires: trigger snapshot of reservation allocation; if spike correlates to a single tenant, manually escalate to bounded-fence mode for that tenant and notify SRE.

Dependencies: autoscaler hooks (ENG-70212), reservation allocator metrics (ENG-71803), console dashboard wiring (PM-412), and billing quota mapping (billing team).

Deliverables: design doc, runtime admission controller changes, allocator adapter, canary rollout plan, dashboards, and post-canary validation report.
acceptance_criteria: No cluster-level eviction spike > 10x baseline during 7-day canary
P95 latency for generation endpoints <= baseline * 1.15 during canary
No customer-facing errors tied to quota enforcement in canary tenants
Dashboards and alerts for eviction_count, reservation_utilization, and burst_volatility_score in place before rollout
Automated rollback triggers configured for 25% production rollout
rollout_plan: Unit + integration tests + canary infra - week 2
Canary deploy to single dedicated cluster with ~30 tenants - week 3 (7 day observation)
Analyze canary metrics and iterate - week 4
Gradual production rollout to 25% clusters with automatic rollback - week 5
